text:
Jules: Heads-up — starting ~09:28 PST we saw a spike of 502/504s hitting hosted inference in us-west-2. Customers report transient failures for streaming completions, lots of errors with trace id prefix abc123... :eyes:
Seema: got the alert. Can you paste a sample client trace ID + a curl or SDK request so we can correlate? Any pattern (large payloads, streaming, embeddings)?
Jules: one sample trace id: abc123-0001. Most failing calls are streaming chat completions from a single tenant, long-lived sessions (~30-120s). Repro curl (reduced):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
```
Ben: looking at ingress logs — Envoy shows upstream resets and HTTP/1.1 protocol errors around the same timeframe. snippets: 
```
[envoy] upstream response reset: reason=CONNECTION_FAILURE, host=model-router-2, trace=abc123-0001
[nginx] 502 while reading response header from upstream, client 10.2.1.5, server api
```
Matt: also seeing repeated `stream closed` on the backend side. A couple of model-router pods reported OOM kill earlier but restarted. Not enough to explain global spike.
Alice: asked product to temporarily route traffic for that tenant to a lower-concurrency pool. Did that at 09:45 — customers reported fewer hard failures but latency up.
InfraBot: auto-scaling triggered +2 ingress nodes at 09:46 due to connection queue depth > 75%.
Seema: hypothesis — connection pool exhaustion / long-lived streaming sessions keeping HTTP/1.1 connections open, causing new requests to get queued and eventually 502/504 from Envoy/nginx when upstream can't accept or times out. Need to check keepalive/idle settings and http2 pool sizing.
Ben: I grep'd the upstream logs — many `reset by peer` from the model side with code `RST_STREAM` and occasional `PROTOCOL_ERROR` from http2. Also saw `downstream_rq_timeout` in envoy for requests waiting > 30s.
Jules: repro steps for us: run 50 concurrent streaming sessions with payloads that hold the stream open (we used wrk2 + custom client). Example stress command we used: 
```
# simplified pseudo-command
stress-client --concurrency 50 --stream-duration 60 --endpoint https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat --token $TOKEN
```
Matt: I pushed a quick config tweak to increase `upstream_connection_pool_size` and bumped Envoy `max_connections_per_host` on the ingress for that AZ. Also increased `idle_timeout` for upstream connections from 15s -> 60s so connections can be reused by streaming sessions.
Seema: good call. We should also enable HTTP/2 multiplexing aggressively for model-router -> model-host to avoid 1:1 connection limits.
Ben: after the changes at 09:47 we see 502/504 rate drop by ~80% in the next 10 minutes. Still a few timeouts for the longest streams but overall stable.
SupportBot: support ticket SUP-2345 opened for affected tenant, customer notified and asked to provide any client-side retry/backoff settings.
Jules: customer said they have immediate fix-ready on their side to lower concurrent streams, but asked for an RCA because it impacts SLAs.
Seema: follow-ups: 1) add metrics for connection pool utilization (idle_conn_count, active_conn_count, pending_requests) and expose them in Console; 2) add an alert when connection queue depth > X for > 5m; 3) evaluate default Envoy circuit-breaker settings and per-tenant qps caps for streaming.
Alice: ops plan — we will backport the pool size and idle_timeout changes to other regions, add an ingress autoscale policy to react faster, and schedule a blameless postmortem.
Ben: note for engineering — model-router needs to gracefully refuse new streams when overloaded instead of hard-resetting connections. I'll open a ticket to add a 503 path with a Retry-After header and instrument it.
Matt: also adding client-facing guidance to SDK docs: recommend HTTP/2 and connection reuse, set streaming timeouts, and exponential backoff for retries (idempotency not guaranteed for streams so caution wording).
Seema: root cause (preliminary) — long-lived streaming sessions + insufficient upstream connection pooling leading to queueing and downstream timeouts/resets under bursty concurrency. Fix was configuration + scaling; longer-term mitigations above.
Jules: monitoring looks stable now; keeping an eye for 24h and then will close the ticket. Thanks all. :+1:
InfraBot: scheduled a follow-up runbook item: "ingress streaming surge" to be added to runbooks repo.
Alice: assigning the postmortem owner to Ben, target within 72 hours.
Jules: closing thread for now — will reopen if errors recur.
